SECTION  20  LABOR  MANAGEMENT  ROUNDT  ABLE  COMMITTEE

  At the request  of any party  and at least proposed  by the Personnel  Officer  on a quarterly  basis,
  the parties  shall convene  a Labor Management  Roundtable  Committee  comprising  of at least
  one member  of each of the City's recognized  labor associations  to address  issues of concern  to
  all parties  and,  if necessary  to address  concerns  specific  to one  association,  to convene  a
  subcommittee  meeting  following  the joint  Labor  Management  Roundtable  Committee.  The
  purpose  of the Labor Management  Committee  meetings  shall be to discuss issues of interest  to
  employees,  issues of interest  to management,  issues of mutual  interest,  and to provide  insight
  to all members  of planned  or proposed  changes  affecting  employee  working  conditions.

  At least  one week  in advance  of the  schedule  meeting,  associations  shall  provide  topics  for
  discussion  at the  Labor  Management  Roundtable  Committee  to permit  time  for  parties  to
  prepare  for a discussion;  however,  members  in attendance  may bring up any topic for discussion
  during  the meeting.  A summary  agenda  will be provided  by management  with  bullet  points  of
  items  to  discuss,  the  last  of which  shall  be "discussion  of  non-agendized  matters."  Each
  association  is permitted  to send at least two  members,  the  preference  of which  is that  the
  President  and Vice President  of each association  should  attend.  If it is necessary  that  additional
  association  members  attend,  at least one week  in advance,  the  association  shall  inform  the
  Personnel  Officer  of that  need  and  Personnel  Officer  should  accommodate  any reasonable
  request  based on the articulated  need for more than two members  of the association  to attend.

  If, during  the Labor  Management  Roundtable  Committee,  it becomes  apparent  that  there  are
  issues specific  to one association  to address  with  the City separately,  the affected  association
  shall request  such a meeting,  which  shall occur  immediately  following  the general  session of the
  Labor  Management  Roundtable  Committee  or within  one calendar  week thereafter,  as agreed
  between  the parties.

  It is encouraged  that  any issues that  arise involving  the Association  are addressed  as soon as
  practicable  by meeting  with  the  Personnel  Officer.  It is recognized  that  most  issues  can be
  resolved  quickly  and informally  using this approach  rather  than  waiting  for the  more  formal
  Labor Management  Roundtable  Committee  to convene.

SECTION  3  MERIT  BASED  INCREASES

  All employees will be placed on the same evaluation schedule with either annual or semi-
  annual evaluations. Advancement to a higher Step in each Grade will be contingent upon
  an overall satisfactory or exemplary performance evaluation. Merit increases must be
  recommended by the employee's Department Head and approved by the City Manager.
  Should a Department Head fail to complete an evaluation through no fault of the
  employee, the employee will automatically  receive any regularly scheduled increase.
  Department Heads are required to take affiri'native  action to withhold a salary step
  increase, with this action to be approved by the City Manager. The withholding of a salary
  step increase may be reviewed by the Personnel Officer ifthe employee requests. Further,
  if a supervisor rates an employee unsatisfactory and fails to withhold a step increase, the
  supervisor shall be required to justify the lack of action. Withholding a salary increase is
  an administrative action, and not disciplinary, and therefore is not a subject to appeal.
  When an employee is given an unsatisfactory performance evaluation and a salary step
  withheld, the employee and the supervisor shall meet and establish goals and a plan to
  improve the performance. When an employee meets the goals of the performance
  improvement plan the employee will then earn a step increase.

SECTION  7  FAMILY  MEDICAL  LEAVE  ACT

  Pursuant  to State & Federal  law, the City  will  provide  family  and medical  care leave  to
  eligible  employees.  The following  provisions  set forth  employees'  rights  and obligations
  with  respect  to sick leave.  Rights  and obligations  that are not specifically  set forth below
  are set in the Department  of Labor  regulations  implementing  the Federal  Family  and
  Medical  Leave  Act  of  1993  (FMLA),  and  the  regulations  of  the  California  Fair
  Employment  and Housing  Commission  implementing  the California  Family  Rights  Act
  (CFRA).  Unless  otherwise  provided  by this section,  "Leave"  under  this provision  shall
  mean  leave pursuant  to the FMLA  and CFRA.

  A.  Amount  of Leave  - Eligible  employees  are entitled  to a total  of 480 hours  of leave
  during  any 12-month  period.  An  employee's  entitlement  to leave  for the birth  or
  placement  of a child  for adoption  or foster  care expires  12 months  after the birth  or
  placement.  The 12-month  period  for calculating  leave entitlement  will  be a "rolling
  period"  measured  backward  from  the date leave  is taken  and continues  with  each
  additional  leave  day taken.  Thus,  whenever  an employee  requests  leave,  the City
  will  look  back over the previous  12-month  period  to determine  how much  leave has
  been used in deterinining  how much  leave a member  is entitled  to.

SECTION  8  BEREAVEMENT

  Employees  shall be allowed  time off for the death of an iinmediate  family  member,  which
  may be taken any time within  ninety  (90) days of the family  member's  passing.  This time
  may be taken non-consecutively  at the discretion  of the employee.  The ten'n "irni'nediate
  family"  is defined  as the spouse,  domestic  partner,  child,  parent,  sibling,  grandparent,
  grandchild,  or parent-in-law  of the employee  or other person  as approved  by the City
  Manager  or his/her  designee.

  Upon  providing  documentation  of  the  death  of  an immediate  family  member,  the
  employee  shall be entitled  to forty  (40) hours  of bereavement  leave,  not chargeable  to
  any other leave. If an employee  does not provide  documentation  of death, the employee's
  time  off shall be chargeable  first  as sick leave and then to any other remaining,  accrued
  leave balance.  If the employee  uses the bereavement  leave consecutively  and wishes  to
  extend that leave to another  forty  (40) hours, he/she may take such additional  consecutive
  leave chargeable  as sick leave.

  Documentation  of  death  must  be provided  within  30 days  of  the  first  day  of  the
  employee's  bereavement  leave.  Such documentation  includes,  but is not limited  to, a
  death certificate,  obituary,  or written  verification  of death,  burial,  or memorial  service
  from  a mortuary,  funeral  home,  burial  society,  crematorium,  religious  institution,  or
  government  agency.  The City  shall keep this documentation  confidential  and shall not
  disclose  it except  as necessary  to internal  personnel  or counsel,  or if required  by law.
  Failure  to provide  documentation  will  result  in any time  off to be charged  against  the
  employee's  sick leave and then to any other remaining,  accrued  leave balance.

SECTION  9  JOB  RELATED  INJURY  OR ILLNESS

  In the event  of an absence  due to a job  related  injury  or illness,  any employee  who  is
  entitled  to disability  payments  under Workers'  Compensation  laws shall receive  from the
  City the difference  between  such disability  payments  and his/her  full salary  for the period
  of absence  up to a maximum  of four  hundred  eighty  (480)  hours  for any one injury  or
  illness.  This  period  of  four  hundred  eighty  (480)  hours  shall  not  be deducted  from
  accumulated  sick leave.  However,  any relapse  at a later  date shall not be compensable
  under  this provision,  although  the same may be chargeable  against  accumulated,  unused
  sick leave, if any.

   B.  Disciplinary  Action

  The  Personnel  Officer  or appropriate  appointing  autliority  may  take  disciplinary
  action  against  an employee  for one or more  of the causes for discipline  specified
  herein  above  in 1.A.  The term "disciplinary  action,"  shall be limited  in meaning  to
  any of the following:

  1.  Demotion,  Discharge,  or Reduction  in Salary
  Such disciplinary  action  may take the form  of discharge,  reduction  in salary,  or
  demotion  where  there  is a vacancy  in the same classification  series  at a lower
  level within  the department.

  2.  Suspension
  An appointing  authority  may suspend  an employee  for one or more of the causes
  for discipline  specified  in these rules for a period  of up to thirty  (30) days.

  3.  Reprimand  and Warnings
  A written  reprimand  or written  warning  is part of the disciplinary  process  when
  an action  or series of actions  by an employee  does not warrant  discipline  as noted
  in sections  B.1 and B.2, however  does warrant  written  notification  for corrective
  purposes.  A  Supervisor  (or  appropriate  management  personnel)  may  issue  a
  written  reprimand  or written  warning  to an employee  for  one or more  of the
  causes for discipline  specified  in these rules. Written  reprimands  and/or  written
  warnings  are not subject  to any appeal or grievance.

SECTION  2  PROBLEM  RESOLUTION

  A.  General  Policy
  It is the policy  of the City to encourage  employees  to resolve  work-related  problems
  at the  earliest  possible  opportunity;  and  for  management  employees  to  assist
  employees  in the timely  solution  of problems  whenever  possible.  For almost  any
  work-related  problem,  employees  are urged  to talk with  their  immediate  supervisor
  first to try to resolve  the problem  before  taking  further  action.  This  section  is for the
  purpose  of specifying  procedures  for  solving  problems,  providing  guidelines  for
  disciplinary  and dismissal  actions  and detailing  methods  by which  employees  may
  appeal  actions  that they believe  are unjust  or unwarranted.

  B.  Non-Disciplinary  Problems
  1.  Compensation  Problems  - Employees  who have any problems  with  their pay or
  benefits,  should  report  it  to  their  departmental  office  immediately  upon
  discovery.  A problem  regarding  a paycheck  should  be reported  no later than ten
  (10)calendardaysafterreceiptofthepaycheck.  IftheactionrequiresPersonnel
  Office  adjustments,  the  department  representative  will  contact  the Personnel
  Office  to resolve  the problem.
  2.  Workers'  Compensation  Problems  - Employees  who  feel they  are not receiving
  the workers'  compensation  benefits  for which  they  qualify,  should  contact  the
  Personnel  Department,  which  will  contact  the  City's  workers'  compensation
  administrator.  Many  questions  can be cleared  up with  a telephone  call.

   3.  Insurance,  Benefits  or Retirement  Problems  - Employees  who  have  a problem
  regarding  any of the City's  insurance  or benefits  or want information  regarding
  retirement,  should  contact  the Personnel  Office.
  4.  Other  Non-Disciplinary  Work  Related  Problems  - Any  problem  not otherwise
  covered  in this section  that an employee  is unable  to resolve  through  informal
  means may be submitted  for resolution  through  the grievance  procedure.
  5.  Interpretation  of Memorandum  of Understanding  Provisions  Employees  who
  have  a problem  that  relates  to  a provision  in  or  an interpretation  of  this
  Memorandum  of Understanding,  should  contact  the Association.  If the problem
  is  not  resolved  through  informal  discussions,  the  Association  may  file  a
  grievance.

  1.  Working  Days  - The  "working  day"  shall  be considered  for  administrative

SECTION  3  GRIEVANCE  PROCEDURE

  A.  Scope

  This  Grievance  Procedure  shall be the exclusive  means  for resolving  all grievances  as
  that term is defined  hereinabove  except  that the following  disputes  shall not be subject
  to the provisions  thereof:
  1.  Any  dispute  arising  out of or in connection  with  meeting  and conferring
  pursuant  to Resolution  No. 3674.
  2.  Any  dispute  arising  in or from,  or involving  a strike,  work  stoppage  or
  cessation  of work  in any form  by employees  of the City.

  B.  Procedure

  STEP  I
  A grievance  may be initiated  in this Step by an employee  or group  of employees  by
  presenting  the grievance  orally  to the immediate  supervisor  of the employee  or
  employees  involved.  The  grievance  must  be submitted  to said supervisor  within
  fifteen  (15)  working  days  following  the occurrence  of the event  upon  which  the
  grievance  is based.  The  supervisor  will  give  an oral  answer  to the employee  or
  employees  involved  within  no  more  than  fi'fteen  (15)  working  days  after  the
  grievance  was orally  presented.

  29

  296
 STEP  2
If the grievance  remains  unresolved  after Step 1, the grievance  may be moved  to Step
2 by submitting  the same to the Department  Head.  The grievance  shall be submitted
in writing  on a form  supplied  by the City.  The grievance  must be submitted  in Step
2 no later than five (5) working  days after the answer  in Step 1 has been received  or
the time  for such answer  has expired.  Within  no more  than five  (5) working  days
a'fter receipt  of grievance,  a meeting  will  be held with  the Department  Head and the
employee  or employees  involved.  A representative  of the employee  or employees
may be present  if requested.  Grievances  submitted  in Step 2 sliall  be answered  in
writing  within  five (5) working  days of said meeting.

STEP  3
1.  If the grievance  remains  unresolved  after  Step 2, the grievance  shall be moved
  immediately  by the Department  Head or the employee  or employees  involved  to
  Step  3 by  submitting  a copy  of the written  form  provided  in  Step  2 to the
  Personnel  Officer.
2.  Within  no more than five (5) working  days after receipt  of the written  grievance,
  a meeting  shall be scheduled  between  the Personnel  Officer  and the employee  or
  employees  involved.  A representative  of the employee  or employees  may  be
  present  if requested.
3.  Grievances  involving  a dispute  between  the City  and the Association  may  be
  initiated  in this Step by either  party  in said written  form  within  five  (5) working
  days of the occurrence  of the event giving  rise to the grievance.  In that event,  a
  meeting  shall be scheduled  within  five (5) working  days of receipt  of said written
  grievance  between  no more  than two (2) designated  representatives  of the City
  and two (2) of the Association.  In addition,  the employee  or employees  involved,
  if any, the Department  Head shall be entitled  to be present  at the meeting.
4.  Grievances  submitted  in Step 3 shall be answered  by the Personnel  Officer  in
  writing  within  five (5) working  days of said meeting(s).

STEP  4
If the dispute  remains  unresolved  after Step 3, the aggrieved  party  can request  final
binding  Arbitration  under  the rules  of the American  Arbitration  Association.  Each
party  will  pay their  own legal  costs. The City  and the employee  will  share the costs
of the American  Arbitration  Association  equally.

General  Definitions
1.  Employee  Representative  - The employee  "representative"  referred  to in Steps 2
  and 3 above may be an employee  of the City.
2.  Grievance  Defined  - Grievance  means any dispute  or difference  between  the City
  and  any  employee  or  group  of  employees,  concerning  the interpretation  or
  application  of any written  City  ordinance,  resolution,  rule,  policy,  practice  or
  procedure  governing  the  wages,  hours  and  working  conditions  of  City
  employees.  The  term  "grievance"  also  includes  any  dispute  or  difference
  between  the City and the Association  concerning  the interpretation  or application
  of  any  existing  memorandum  of  understanding  between  the  City  and  the
  Association.

 At the request  of any party  and at least proposed  by the Personnel  Officer  on a quarterly  basis, the

 member  of each of the City's  recognized  labor  associations  to address  issues  of concern  to all

Management  Roundtable  Committee  or within  one calendar  week  thereafter,  as agreed  between
the parties.

quickly  and informally  using  this  approach  rather  than  waiting  for  the  more  formal  Labor

   ARTICLE  VII
  LAYOFF  PROCEDURES
SECTION  1.  LAYOFF  PROCEDURES

  1.1  Layoff

  The City  Council  or City Manager  may separate any employee  or class of positions
  without  prejudice,  because of financial  or economic  condition  of the City,  reduction
  of work,  or abandonment  of activities.  If the reduction  in force  is necessary  for
  economic  reasons,  as a general  law city,  the City  shall  observe  the seniority  rule
  per Government  Code Section 45100 in putting the reduction  into effect. The City
  shall give employees  covered by this MOU not less than fifteen (15) calendar days
  advance notice of lay-off and the reason therefore. However,  no full-time  employee
  shall be separated from a department  while regular part-time  or hourly employees
  are serving in the same positions  in the department.

  1.2  Bumping  Rights

  The employee  laid-off  shall be entitled  to bump  to the position  in a class in which
  they currently  or formerly  held a permanent  appointment  and in which  there is an
  employee  with  less seniority  in the class, if physically  and mentally  able to perform
  the duties of the former class. After the City has notified the affected
  employee and
  also the position  available  to the employee,  if any, to bump, they must notify the
  Persoru'iel Officer of their intent to exercise the bumping  rights within fourteen (14)
  calendar days of the position  and classification  in the City which they intend to
  bump, or the bumping  rights shall be barred and waived to the employee.  The
  employee with the least seniority  in the class shall be bumped by the person who is
  laid off. The employee bumped shall be considered  as laid-off for the same reason
  as the person  who bumped  them  and shall in the same manner be eligible to bump
  to a position  in a class within  the City in which they formally  had a permanent
  position.

  1.3  Appointment  of Laid-Off  Employees  to Lower  Class

  The City Manager  may approve  the appointment  of an employee  who is to be laid-
  off  to an existing  vacancy  in a lower  class for which  they  are qualified  without
  requiring  an  examination,  provided  the  appropriate  appointing  authority  so
  appoints.

This comprehensive Memorandum of Understanding (hereinafter 'MOU"  or ".Agreemerxt") is
made  and entered  into between  the South  Gate Police  Officers'  Association,  hereinafter  referred
to as the "Association,"  and the City  of South Gate, hereinafter  referred  to as the "City,"  pursuant

individual  MOUs  and side agreements  into this one comprehensive  document.  It is possible  that
provisions  ofthe  MOUs  and/or  side agreements  orrelated  agreements  may have been inadvertently
omitted  in the comprehensive  MOU.  Therefore,  each party  to this MOU  reserves  its rights  to bring
to the other party's  attention  a provision  in a prior  MOU  or still valid  side agreement  or resolution
that is not included  in this MOU.  In such case, the parties  agree to convene  meetings  to address
the issue and to engage in good faith  attempts  to reach agreement  as to the validity  and/or  content
of any such omitted  evidence  of ten'ns and conditions  of employment.  No representation  is made
that such agreement(s)  shall be arrived  at.

Additionally,  in preparing  this  MOU,  it is not the intent  of the parties  to invalidate  terms  and
conditions  of employment  that are not set forth  in this MOU,  but which  are referenced  in a still
valid  side agreement  or past practice  as this term is defined  by statutory  and case law.

The sections  described  herein  may reference  dates in parentheses.  Those dates are indicative  of the
particular  MOU  or side agreement  from  which  the substance  of the section  is derived.  Said dates
are included  for reference  purpose  only.

SECTION  4. BEREAVEMENT  LEAVE

Employees  shall be allowed  time off for the death of an immediate  family  member,  which  may be
taken  any time  within  ninety  (90) days of the family  member's  passing.  This  time  may be taken
non-consecutively  at the discretion  of the employee.  The term "immediate  family"  is defined  as
the spouse,  domestic  partner,  child,  parent,  sibling,  grandparent,  grandchild,  or parent-in-law  of
the employee  or other person  as approved  by the City  Manager  or his/her  designee.

Upon  providing  documentation  of the death of an irnrnediate  family  member,  the employee  shall
be entitled  to forty  (40)  hours  of bereavement  leave,  not  chargeable  to any other  leave.  If an
employee  does not provide  documentation  of death,  the employee's  time  off shall be chargeable
first as sick leave and then to any other remaining,  accrued  leave balance.  If the employee  uses the
bereavement  leave consecutively  and wishes  to extend that leave to another  forty  (40) hours, he/she
may  take such additional  consecutive  leave chargeable  as sick leave.

Documentation  of death  must  be provided  within  30 days  of the first  day of the employee's
bereavement  leave. Such documentation  includes,  but is not limited  to, a death certificate,  obituaiy,
or written  verification  of death, burial,  or memorial  service  from  a mortuary,  funeral  home,  burial
society,  crematorium,  religious  institution,  or government  agency.  The  City  shall  keep  this
documentation  confidential  and shall not disclose  it except  as necessary  to internal  persoru'iel  or
counsel,  or if required  by law. Failure  to provide  documentation  will  result  in any time  off to be
charged  against the employee's  sick leave and then to any other remaining,  accrued  leave balance.

  grandchild, or parent-in-law of the employee or other person as approved by the City
  Manager  or his/her designee.

  employee shall be entitled to forty (40) hours of bereavement leave, not chargeable to any
  other leave. If an employee does not provide documentation of death, the employee's time

  balance. If the employee uses the bereavement leave consecutively and wishes to extend
  that leave to another forty (40) liours, he/she may take such additional consecutive leave
  chargeable as sick leave.

CONSOLIDATED  SALARY  SCHEDULE  FOR  ALL  FULL-TIME  EMPLOYEES  AND

PURPOSE:  To approve  and adopt  an updated  consolidated  pay schedule  for all full-time  and
selected  part-time  employees  within  the  California  Public  Employee  Retirement  System
(CalPERS)  guidelines.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  approving
and  adopting  an updated  consolidated  pay  schedule  for  all  full-time  and  selected  part-time
employees  within  the CalPERS  guidelines.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the Fiscal  Year 2025-2026  Adopted  Budget.

ANALYSIS:  None.

BACKGROUND:  During  the course  of the current  fiscal  year,  there  have been several  pay

adjustments  resulting  from  labor  agreements,  state law  mandates,  contract  negotiations,  budget
approvals  and reevaluations  of pay, the latest  of which  was the approval  of the City's  employee
Associations'  MOUs  and  the  Terms  and  Conditions  of  Employment  of  the  Unrepresented
Executive  Management  Group.  The  attached  consolidated  salary  schedule  reflects  all changes
made to employees'  salaries  and wages  since the beginning  of Fiscal  Year  2025/26.

The consolidated  salary  schedule  under  consideration  of approval  by the City  Council  contains  the
3.0% cost-of-living  wage increases  to all full-time  employees  with  an effective  date of September
7, 2025,  and an adjustment  in the full-time  equivalent  part-time  positions  to ensure their  hourly
rates remain  in parity  with  their  :[ull-time  counterparts  with  an effective  date of October  5, 2025,
or the first  day of the first  full  pay  period  following  approval  and adoption  of this  proposed
resolution.

Additionally,  there  is correction  of Life  Guard,  Swim  Instructor,  and Senior  Life  Guard  hourly
rates to be tied to the Recreation  Leader  series of job classifications  and, therefore,  these positions

  1

  384
 are retitled  to Recreation  Leader  II (Life  Guard),  Recreation  Leader  III  (Swim  Instructor),  and
Recreation  Leader  IV (Senior  Life  Guard).

Further,  CalPERS,  pursuant  to its interpretation  of the California  Code of Regulations  €3)570.5  of
the Public  Employees'  Retirement  Law  (PERL),  as outlined  in its January  8, 2020 Circular  Letter,
recommends  that  all  CalPERS  employers  maintain  their  compensation  levels  in one publicly
available  document,  approved  and adopted  by the governing  body,  which  must  meet  all of the
following  criteria:

  1)  Hasbeendulyapprovedandadoptedbytheemployer'sgoverningbodyinaccordancewith
  the requirements  of applicable  public  meetings  laws;
  2)  Identifies  the position  title  for every  employee  position;
  3)  Shows  the pay rate for each identified  position,  which  may be stated as a single  amount  or
  as multiple  amounts  within  a range;
  4)  Indicates  the time base, including,  but not limited  to, whether  the time base is hourly,  daily,
  bi-weekly,  monthly,  bi-monthly,  or annually;
  5)  Is posted  at the office  of the employer  or immediately  accessible  and available  for public
  review  from  the  employer  during  normal  business  hours  or posed  on the  employer's
  internet  website;
  6)  Indicates  an effective  date and date of any revisions;
  7)  Is retained  by the employer  and available  for public  inspection  for not less than five years;
  and
  8)  Does not reference  another  document  in lieu of disclosing  the pay rate.

Under  the PERL  and the Public  Employees'  Pension  Reform  Act  of 2013  (PEPRA),  earnable
compensation  and pensionable  compensation  are determined  in accordance  with  the  amounts
identified  on a publicly  available  pay schedule  as adopted  and approved  by the City  Council.  If an
employer  were to fail  to meet with  requirements  of Section  570.5  as stated  above,  the CalPERS
Board  may  determine  at its sole discretion  an amount  that will  be considered  as a pay rate in
determining  what  a retiree's  earnable  income  will  be, which  will  never  be higher  than the amount
stated  on the comprehensive  salary  schedule.  As a result,  publicly  available  pay schedules  are
required  by  CalPERS  and  are a critical  component  to  veri:ty  all  members'  pay  rates  when
calculating  members'  retirement  benefits.  Finally,  maintaining  a compliant  publicly  available  pay
schedule  will  support  transparency  and expedite  CalPERS'  review  process.  Failure  to provide
CalPERS  with  a compliant  publicly  available  pay schedule  may result in a retirement  benefit  being
delayed  and/or  reduced.

Therefore,  the purpose  of approving  this resolution  is to update  the current  Consolidated  Salary
Schedule  to reflect  the changes  as authorized  by the City Council  in this agenda item and to comply
with  the PERL.

 FISCAL IMPACT:  To fund the Principal Accountant in the Administrative Services Department,
no additional appropriate is requested. The position will be funded with existing appropriations:
base salary/benefits from the budgeted Senior Accountant with any difference in FY 2025-26
covered  by vacancy  salary  savings.

To fund the Transportation and Capital Improvement Program Division Manager and the Water
Resources and Development Division Manager position in the Public Works Department,  the FY
2025-26 Adopted Budged downsized the Engineering Division from three divisions to two and
eliminated the Deputy City Engineer position. Savings from that elimination, along with related
adjustments approved in the budget, fund the two Division Manager reclassifications. Net General

 BACKGROUND:  The City must, from time to time, add, remove, reclassify, or otherwise adjust
job classifications, job specifications and/or compensation in the Salaty Resolution and Position
 Classification Plan to satisfy the changing needs and demands of the City's workforce. In response
to these changing needs and demands, job classification specifications must be amended to more
 closely match the tasks which need to be performed by employees in the City's various
departments.

Administrative  Services staff, Human Resources and the City Manager evaluated the needs and
structure of the Administrative  Services Department and are recommending the creation  of the
full-time Principal Accountant, which is an exempt position assigned to the Professional Mid-
Management Association.  The Principal Accountant  will be paid from $8,468/month  to
$10,293/month. The Principal Accountant will lead day-to-day Citywide accounting operations,
and financial reporting, will supervises professional and technical accounting staff (e.g., general
ledger/financial  reporting, accounts payable/receivable,  payroll interface/reconciliation,  fixed
assets, grants, project/cost accounting), will manage the month-end and year-end close, will
coordinate external audit fieldwork and produces the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report
(ACFR) and related regulatory reports, will ensure compliance with GAAP/GASB  and internal
controls, and will perform other related duties.

As part ofthe City Council's approval of the City's FY 2025/26 Adopted Budget, the Public Works
Department's Engineering Division was reorganized and downsized from three divisions to two
through the elimination of the Deputy City Engineer position, the freezing of one (1) Principal
Civil Engineer position, and downgrading  to three (3) Assistant Engineers. To absorb these
changes, responsibilities  were consolidated: the Traffic Engineering Section was expanded to
oversee the full Capital Improvement Program, while the Water Resources Section was expanded
to include Development Services. To manage these broader scopes, the two Division Manager
positions were created by rescoping the former City Traffic Engineer and Principal Civil Engineer
(Water Resources) roles. This restructuring streamlines operations, ensures proper oversight of
expanded responsibilities, and it reduces overall General Fund costs.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  SIMPLER  SYSTEMS.  INC.  FOR  FINANCIAL
REPORTING  SOFTWARE  LICENSING  AND  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES

PURPOSE:  To  approve  a Professional  Services  Agreement  with  Simpler  Systems,  Inc.
("Simpler")  to accelerate  financial  reporting,  audit  support,  and budget  development  in the City's
Tyler  Eden environment.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Professional  Services  Agreement  with  Simpler,  to provide  financial  reporting
  software  ("Simpler  Platform")  and  related  professional  services  with  a not-to-exceed
  amount  of $51,380  (License  $17,500 + Professional  Services  $30,800  + 10% contingency
  $3,080),  and ongoing  Monthly  License  & Maintenance  of $1,750  (aru"iualized  $21,000),
  subject  to annual  appropriation.
  b.  Authorizing  the issuance  of a Purchase  Order  to Simpler,  by a sole-source  determination
  based on proprietary  functionality  and its "datapps"  architecture  and market  uniqueness  for
  Eden-based  financial  reporting,  pursuant  to SGMC  § 1.54.510.
  c.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement,  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  Approval  authorizes  $51,380  in  one-time  costs  (License  $17,500;
Professional  Services  $30,800;  10%  contingency  $3,080)  and  ongoing  $1,750/month
($21,000/year)  for License  & Maintenance.  Funding  will  be appropriated  from  the Information
Technology  Fund and recorded  in Account  No. 522-305-12-6101;  ongoing  costs will  be budgeted
in future  fiscal  years.

BACKGROUND:  The City  uses Tyler  Eden for core financials.  While  Eden and a library  of ad-
hoc  Crystal  Reports  have  supported  daily  operations  and  audits,  both  are labor-intensive  to
maintain  and adapt.  Each  chart-of-accounts  change  (e.g.,  new  funds  or object  codes)  requires
manual  report  edits and re-testing,  and many  outputs  still need hand formatting  for departments  or
auditors.  The City  has no in-house  specialist  for generating  Crystal  Reports,  creating  a bottleneck

  1

  399
 and schedule risk, and requires the hiring of contractors to assist with Crystal Report  development
and troubleshooting.

Because  Eden's  native  reports  and Crystal  Reports  outputs  are not optimized  for flexible  analysis,
staff spend significant  time  extracting,  reshaping,  and reconciling  data for routine  monthly  closes,
budget development,  and audit requests.  This  slows  decision-making  and increases  reliance  on a
few technical users.

Simpler  provides  a browser-based  reporting  layer that unlocks  Eden data for self-service  analysis
and standardized  financial  statements.  It delivers  roll-ups  with  drill-down  to transactions  in a
format  that departments  and auditors  can use without  custom  coding.  Simpler  can also serve as the
repository  for historical  Eden  data during  any future  ERP transition,  preserving  continuity  and
minimizing  change-management  impacts  when the City  migrates  platforms.

ANALYSIS:  Simpler  will  provide  an enterprise  (unlimited-user)  license  for  Eden-focused
"datapps,"  including  Statements  & Summaries  (with  budget),  Transactions,  Purchasing/Payables,
Vendors,  and Budget.  Services  include  installation/configuration,  limited  customization,  training,
and ongoing  support.

For over  25 years,  Simpler  has specialized  in governrnent  finance  reporting  and adjacent  data
domains  (e.g., utility  billing,  permitting,  HR, public  safety).  The product  is designed  from  an end-
user perspective-templates  and filters  reflect  how  finance  and departments  consume  data-so
users can navigate  from  summary  views  to entry-level  detail  with  minimal  training.  Vendor  staff
build  and validate  queries  with  the City's  data, reducing  rework  and accelerating  adoption.

Key advantages:
  *  Automatically  adapts  to new  Chart  of Accounts  codes and values-no  recurring  Crystal
  Reports  rewrites.
  *  Near real-time,  self-service  access-fewer  ad hoc data pulls  or report  tickets.
  *  Intuitive  UI-low  training  overhead;  broad  adoption  outside  Finance.
  *  Reduces  single-point-of-failure  risk-knowledge  is embedded  in the tool,  not one report
  writer.
  *  Drill-down  from  statements  to transaction  detail  to validate  anomalies  quickly.
  *  Simple  export  and sharing-PDF/Excel/CSV  and URL  links  for point-in-time  views.
  *  100%  browser-based-no  desktop  installs;  minimal  IT support  required.

Sole  Source  Determination.  Staff  recommends  the City  Council  waive  the RFP  process  under
Administrative  Regulation  206  (per  SGMC  § 1.54.350)  and  approve  a sole-source  award  to
Simpler  Systems  based on the following:  (1) Simpler  offers  a proprietary,  Eden-specific  reporting
layer  with  unique  compatibility/standardization  advantages  that cannot  be reasonably  replicated
by other vendors  without  materially  greater  cost and effort;  (2) the solution  allows  unlimited  users,
minimal  IT  lift,  and drill-down  to transaction  detail;  and (3) timing  and continuity  needs  for
audit/budget  cycles  favor  this selection  in the City's  best interest.

Finance  staff  expects  immediate  productivity  gains-especially  for  the  annual  audit-by
eliminating  manual  reformatting,  standardizing  auditor-ready  statements,  and  enabling  secure

  400
 read-only  access for external  auditors  as needed.  In the near term,  this can save days to weeks  of
staff effort  across audit and budget  cycles.

6.23  Data  Security;  Breach  Notification.

  (a) Security  Program.  Consultant  shall implement  and maintain  an information  security
  program  aligned  to generally  accepted  standards  (e.g., NIST  CSF and CIS  Critical
  Security  Controls  IGI/IG2)  appropriate  to the nature  of the Services  and City  Data.

  (b) Minimum  Controls.  Controls  shall  include:  multi-factor  authentication  for
  administrative  access;  least-privilege  role-based  access;  endpoint  protection;  secure
  software  development  practices;  quarterly  vulnerability  scanning;  timely  patching  of
  high/critical  vulnerabilities;  change  management;  and  Jogging/monitoring  of
  security-relevant  events for at least 90 days online  and 1 year archived.

  (c) Encryption.  Consultant  shall encrypt  City  Data in transit  (TLS  1.2 or higher)  and at
  rest using  industry-standard  strong  encryption  (e.g., AES-256  or equivalent).

  (d) Hosting  & Network  Security.  Whether  City-  or Consultant-hosted,  environments
  shall  be  segmented,  hardened,  and  regularly  updated.  Default  credentials  are
  prohibited.  Remote  access shall use MFA  and secure protocols  only.

  (e) Backups  &  Continuity.  Consultant  shall  maintain  backups  and  a  business
  continuity/disaster  recovery  plan suitable  for the Services.  Upon  request,  Consultant
  will  disclose  target  RPO/RTO  and test results  summary.

  (f)  Personnel  &  Subprocessors.  Consultant  shall  ensure  personnel  and  approved
  subprocessors  with  access to City  Data are subject  to confidentiality  obligations  and
  receive  security  awareness  training  at least  annually.  Consultant  remains  fully
  responsible  for subprocessors'  compliance.

  (g) Security  Reviews.  Upon  reasonable  notice  (no more  than aru'iually),  Consultant  will
  complete  the  City's  security  questionnaire  and  provide  available  third-party
  attestations  or  summaries  (e.g.,  SOC  2 report  letter,  penetration  test  executive
  summary),  which  may be redacted  for confidentiality.

  (h) Incident  Definition.  A "'Security  Incident"  means any actual  or reasonably  suspected
  unauthorized  access to, acquisition  of, or use, disclosure,  alteration,  or destruction  of

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  ALL  CITY  MANAGEMENT  SERVICES,  INC.,  FOR
CROSSING  GUARD  SERVICES

PURPOSE:  To enter into an agreement  with  All  City  Management  Services,  Inc., for Crossing  Guard
Services  to continue  to provide  for the safety  of students,  parents,  and staff  as they  walk  to and from
school,  and to ensure  that designated  intersections  are controlled  and monitored  during  peak periods  of
pedestrian  presence.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  All  City Management  Services,  Inc. ("ACMS"),  for crossing  guard
  services  for a one (1) year ternn, effective  July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  ACMS  has increased  rates  commensurate  with  the  cost  of  living  and  rising
operational  costs. These  price  increases  are reflected  in an increase  from  $33.94  per hour  in fiscal  year
2024-2025  to $34.80 per hour  in fiscal  year  2025-26.  Funds  of $712,332.72 were  budgeted  from  the
Crossing  Guard  Program  for crossing  guard  services  during  the FY2024-2025  budget  process.  However,
the total  annual  projected  costs  of services  for  this  service  contract,  FY2025-26,  are $730,382.40,  an
increase  of $18,049.68. The increased  costs are reflected  in the hourly  rate increase.

BACKGROUND:  Since August  of 1994,  the City  has contracted  with  All  City  Management  Services,
Inc., to provide  crossing  guard  services  throughout  the City.  The decision  to contract  this operation  was

based on cost savings  and increased  operational  services.  The responsibility  of adequately  staffing  school
crossing  locations,  if a crossing  guard  was unable  to fill  his/her  shift,  was that of the Police  Department
and a sworn  police  officer  would  o'ften be pulled  off the streets  to provide  coverage.  Use of this third
party transfers  staffing  responsibility  and, as such, the department  has been very satisfied  with  the services
provided  by ACMS,

Although  the South  Gate Police  Department  has been satisfied  with  the service  provided  by ACMS,  the
opportunity  to evaluate  similar  services  and pricing  from  another  contractor  was recently  explored.  Staff
conducted  research  and found  that ACMS  is essentially  the only  vendor  in the area that  can provide
services  on the scale required  by the City  of South  Gate. ACMS  has provided  the City  with  outstanding
service  for over 20 years,  as well  as, being  immensely  responsive  to the City's  needs and requests.

Dear Sergeant,

It is once again the time of the year when many agencies are formulating their budgets for the
corning fiscal year. Toward that end, please allow this letter to serve as confirmation of our interest
in extending our agreement for Crossing Guard Services through the 2025-2026 school years.

As you may know, hiring challenges have impacted all sectors of the labor market across the nation.
Recently the United States Chamber of Cornrnerce has published an article "Understanding
America's Labor Shortage", which illustrates how thousands of jobs are published each month and
yet a significant number of positions still remain unfilled. Essentially, labor force participations  rates
have still not returned to pre-COVID levels. This situation leads to heightened competition  among
businesses  as they vie for the limited  pool of available  talent.

ACMS has experienced these same challenges and in many cases, we've transitioned a significant
number of employees from an older, primarily stable workforce to a younger mobile workforce. This
new segment of our employees are more sensitive to current cost-of-living increases and are looking
for higher wages and more hours. They often accept our position and work for days, sometimes
weeks and if we're lucky months then abruptly leave when they find higher pay.

For these reasons, as well as cost increases in most segments of our business, we must appeal for an
increase in our hourly rate for the upcoming 2025-2026 school years. To facilitate the calculation of
the 2025-2026 aru'iual cost of your CrossingGuard program, we have de'veloped and included with
this letter a Client Worksheet. This Worksheet details the new hourly billing rate and the overall
estimated program cost, based on the number of sites and the hours worked at each site.

We remain committed to providing a safe, cost-effective and professional School Crossing Guard
Program and we hope you will find this new pricing acceptable. If you have any questions or need

 -INTRODUCTION

The Gateway  Cities Council of Governments  (GCCOG) subregion consists of 27 cities and additional
unincorporated  communities  in Southeast Los Angeles County, with a total population of just under two
million. The subregion is predominantly  urban and is suited for infill development or redevelopment.
The Gateway Cities are served by a transportation  network that includes major freeways and arterial
roads, light rail lines, and  local transit bus systems, with two additional light rail lines in environmental
review. The subregion is also home to the Port of Long Beach and neighbor to the Port of Los Angeles.
Together, they form the nation's largest marine port complex, and freight moves through the Gateway
Cities by truck and rail. The Los Angeles and San Gabriel rivers also traverse the region from north to
south. The Gateway Cities have collaborated via the GCCOG Joint Powers Authority since the mid-
l990's, on transportation,  air quality, housing, and economic development  issues. For additional
information  about the GCCOG,  please visit www.qatewaycoq.orq.

Gateway Cities was awarded funding from the Southern California Association of Government  (SCAG)
Regional Early Action Program 2.0 (REAP21  ) Subregional  Partnership  Program,  which  is intended  to:
Accelerate Infill Development that Facilitates Housing  Supply,  Choice, and  Affordability;  and
Affirmatively Further Fair Housing; and Reduce Vehicle Miles Traveled.

The GCCOG has selected and entered into master agreements with a bench of consultants to provide
technical assistance to cities to support the development of housing, with a specific focus on the
development of affordable infill housing - both rental and owner-occupied.  The purpose of Gateway
Cities' TA Team is to provide the technical resources that Gateway  Cities need to more easily, quickly,
and efficiently implement the goals, policies and programs included in their 6th cycle housing elements.
This Request for Proposals is being shared with the entire bench of three consultants and one proposal
will be selected to provide the project services.

and rezoned properties northeast of the Firestone Boulevard/Atlantic  Avenue intersection to TV in
anticipation of Metro's plans for a transit center at that location.  In  2019,  the City of South Gate
prepared the Gateway District Specific Plan (GDSP) for the  area  but did  not adopt it because
there was not an inclusionary housing ordinance. The draff GDSP is located here: GATEWAY

minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:45 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Gil
  Hurtado and Council Member Al Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz,
  City Manager Rob Houston, City Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

EXCUSED/ABSENT  Council Member Maria del Pilar Avalos

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  The City Council approved items A & B by motion of Council Member
  Rios and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-28-CC entitled A Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of South Gate, approving the Fiscal Year 2024-2025
  Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (“CAPER”);
  and

  b. Authorized the City Manager, or designee, to submit to the U.S.
  Department of Housing and Urban Development the Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 CAPER.

  Carol Averell, Housing Manager, gave a presentation.

  Council Member Hurtado is disappointed with the continue graffiti and the
  amount of money the city spends for graffiti abatement.

  Council Member Rios questioned if the city would continue applying for
  federal funding.

  Ms. Averell stated that there was an 11% cut for this year for CDBG. The
  city is waiting for the contracts for this fiscal year.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

1
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING CONT’D  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item. Seeing no one step forward; Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused.

2
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  The City Council approved items A & B by motion of Council Member
  Hurtado and seconded by Council Member Rios:

  a. Waived the reading in full and introduced Ordinance No. 2025-01-CC
  entitled An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California amending Title 11, Chapter 11.43 (Accessory Dwelling
  Units and Accessory Structures) of the South Gate Municipal Code;
  and

  b. Accepted the determination that the proposed amendment is Exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) as a
  “ministerial” project pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15268(a).

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, stated Joshua
  Valdez, Associate Planner, will be giving the presentation. This item is
  before City Council because the city has not updated the ADU ordinance
  Accessory Dwelling Units since 2021. There are new laws ever year that
  are passed by the state that amend rules for ADUs across the state and the
  city must comply with the requirements.

  Joshua Valdez, Associate Planner, gave the presentation.

  Vice Mayor Barron thanked Mr. Valdez for the presentation. He stated this
  community is overrun with difficulties with finding parking and the State
  of California is saying there is a housing crisis. He understands the need
  for housing but does not agree to adding more housing.

  Mayor Davia stated the City of South Gate is required to build 8,282 units
  and the city will keep having parking issues.

  Council Member Rios stated that on the governor’s desk is a bill that
  would allow building six-story buildings/housing in neighborhoods which
  would create problems.

  Page 2 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

2
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN CONT’D  Council Member Hurtado stated the City of Jurupa has the same
  population as the City of South Gate and does not understand why the City
  of Jurupa is only required to build 2,400 units and South Gate is required
  to build 8,282 units.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item. Seeing no one step forward; Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council Member Avalos,
  excused.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA Steve Soto thanked Council Member Rios for inviting him tonight. Mr.
  Soto has been writing poems and an author for over 60 years. He has been
  a guest poet columnist for the Desert Sun newspaper. A newspaper that
  serves Palm Springs and the Coachella Valley. Mr. Soto wrote and read a
  poem called “Home of the Brave” in response to unconscionable treatment
  of immigrants.

  South Gate resident informed City Council that he was on his bicycle
  heading eastbound on Santa Ana Street between California and Otis where
  he fell forward due to uneven streets. He is requesting the streets to be
  fixed.

  Carlos Gonzalez, Jr., South Gate resident, is a parent and volunteer and is
  speaking on behalf of the American Youth Soccer Organization, also
  known as AYSO. He informed Council that AYSO practice at Hollydale
  Park and is requesting better lighting.

  Heidi Portillo and her son are present tonight reading a statement prepared
  by all the families in NYSO asking for better lighting at Hollydale Park.

  Sergio Sanchez stated his son play for NYSO. The previous parents
  already spoke on the lighting issues at Hollydale Park, but there are other
  issues, for example the men’s restrooms.

  Mario Sanchez and his children are present tonight. Mr. Sanchez stated his
  children are members of AYSO and having children play sports keeps
  them busy and out of trouble. He reiterated about having better lighting at
  Hollydale Park.

  Consuelo Godoy, South Gate resident, is requesting City Council to place
  a flagpole and a flag in front of city hall in memory of Nicolas “Nick”

  Page 3 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
CONT’D  Godoy. Mr. Godoy was a member of the VFW for 20 years. She stated if
  funds are needed to please inform her.

  Juan Contreras also spoke on the conditions of the restrooms at Hollydale
  Park and poor lighting.

EMAILS  Mario Dominguez, South Gate resident, is requesting the City of South
  Gate develop a bike trail on Southern Avenue like the City of Bellflower.
  He stated South Gate is not bike friendly and the Gate buses lack bike
  racks.

  Claudia Rivera, South Gate resident, is questioning Councilwoman
  Avalo’s character for proposing Robert Montalvo to the Parks
  Commission. Ms. Rivera and her family will no longer support Council
  Members Avalos and Rios.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Mayor Davila asked Mr. Costley about Hollydale Park restrooms.

  Mr. Costley will check on Hollydale Regional Park. He mentioned the
  park is farther away from the community and next to the riverbeds. Every
  time the Parks Department places partition doors, they get stolen. The city
  has put thousands of thousands of dollars into doors. Mr. Costley will
  speak with the restroom industry businesses about new and improved
  doors.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, addressed the condition of the
  sidewalk on Santa Ana.

  Mayor Davila requested the street be looked at.

  Council Member Hurtado explained the process on the non-agenda items.

  Mr. Houston explained the chain of command and asked Mr. Costley if he
  was familiar with the folks that spoke tonight.

  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation, stated yes, the parks
  department has liaison information to the AYSO.

  Mr. Costley thanked everyone that was able to attend the new teen room at
  the girls clubhouse. On October 4th there is the Art Walk in front of the
  auditorium. Everyone is invited to attend the opening of the renovated
  Circle Park at 4 p.m. on October 13th. He also mentioned Fireworks show
  at the Halloween event.

  Page 4 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, no updates.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services, no updates.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, no updates.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police, announced the Third South Gate Annual
  Classic Car Show scheduled for this Saturday at 10 o’clock. He also
  mentioned taking possession of their second Harley-Davidson motorcycle
  courtesy of Office of Traffic Safety.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, informed the public that their comments are
  heard. The AYSO may have a dialogue with the Director of Parks &
  Recreation. He also mentioned the city’s limitations at Hollydale Park due
  to Edison Easement with powerlines.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, nothing to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, mentioned the City Clerk’s Office processes
  passport applications by appointment. Currently the appointments are
  from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and starting this Monday, we will have afternoon
  appointments from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

  Council Member Rios is suggesting AYSO using the LAUSD field or
  exploring other city facilities that have lighting.

  Council Member Rios enjoyed Mr. Soto’s poem. He attended a water
  workshop and stated two thirds of our water comes from Northern
  California. He asked Mr. Costley to speak about the Senior Adult
  Transportation Popup.

  Mr. Costley stated this Friday the city will be connecting the seniors with
  the Metro, local bus and dial-a-ride.

  Council Member Hurtado mentioned the homeless by the riverbed have
  been lighting very loud fireworks. He informed Connie Godoy that Nick
  Godoy was very nice to him. Nick Godoy was a good person. He
  commended the parents for volunteering and having their children in the
  AYSO. He stated speaking to a representative or consultant for the bus
  route regarding bike racks. The consultant stated because the way the bus
  is set up, a permanent rack cannot be placed but will see if a temporary
  rack can be placed.

  Page 5 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Vice Mayor Barron thanked AYSO for attending tonight’s meeting and the
  parents for volunteering.

  Vice Mayor Barron is the President of the SELA Kiwanis and mentioned
  September 30th will be the Second Annual College Fair and Career Fair at
  the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. There will
  be over 27 universities, colleges, and workforce development
  organizations. He thanked Supervisor Janice Hanh and Assembly Member
  Solache for their contribution to the event for the scholarships.

  Vice Mayor Barron mentioned that on October 4th Kiwanis is hosting a car
  show as a fundraiser in the City of Bell Gardens, Ford Park. He had the
  opportunity to visit the Western Carpenters Union Center in Carson. He
  attended an event this weekend for the Save America Movement. Food
  distribution is still being done through the SELA Kiwanis Organization
  and Southeast Leadership Foundation.

  Mayor Davila attended the new teen room and thanked Mr. Costley and
  staff for their hard work putting the room together. She is planning to
  attend the Transportation Popup on Friday and thanked the AYSO parents
  for bringing their concerns to City Council.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were approved by motion of
  Mayor Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Hurtado, yes; Council Member Rios, yes
  (voted no on 5); Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila, yes; Council
  Member Avalos, excused.

3
SURPLUS PERSONAL
PROPERTY MGMT  The City Council approved items A, B & C during Consent Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-29-CC entitled A Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of South Gate declaring the items listed in Attachment B
  (Bicycles & Miscellaneous Items) and Attachment C (Vehicles &
  Equipment) as surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable City personal
  property.

  b. Authorized the City Manager or designee to dispose of the declared
  items through public auction conducted by U.S. Auctions of Ontario,
  CA; and to execute all related documents consistent with budgeted
  appropriations.

  Page 6 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2025

3
SURPLUS PERSONAL
PROPERTY MGMT CONT’D
  c. Authorized the City Manager or designee to dispose of any items not
  accepted by the auctioneer or failing to sell by using one or more of
  the following methods, as appropriate: recycling/salvage, scrap, inter-
  agency transfer, trade-in/credit, donation to another public agency, or
  landfill, in compliance with applicable laws and City policies.
